es.summary: Trastorno neurodegenerativo caracterizado por deterioro cognitivo fluctuante, alucinaciones visuales y síntomas parkinsonianos.
key_points: Fluctuaciones en la atención son más pronunciadas que la pérdida de memoria.
Alucinaciones visuales y trastornos del sueño son signos distintivos.
Los síntomas motores pueden confundirse con enfermedad de Parkinson.
Diagnóstico clínico apoyado por neuroimagen y pruebas de dopamina.
El tratamiento combina inhibidores de colinesterasa y manejo cuidadoso de antipsicóticos.

pathophysiology: Acumulación de cuerpos de Lewy (α‑sinucleína) en neuronas corticales y subcorticales.
Disrupción de neurotransmisores, especialmente dopamina y acetilcolina.
Degeneración neuronal produce déficits cognitivos y síntomas motores.
Fluctuaciones de alerta por alteración de la red reticular activadora.
risk_factors: Sexo masculino con ligera mayor prevalencia.
Antecedentes familiares de demencia o enfermedad de Parkinson.
signs_symptoms: Deterioro cognitivo fluctuante, peor en atención que en memoria.
Trastornos del sueño con movimientos REM sin atonía.
Rigidez, temblor y bradicinesia similares a Parkinson.
diagnostics: Evaluación clínica con MMSE o MoCA y criterios de consenso.
Neuroimagen (MRI/CT) muestra atrofía mínima; SPECT/PET puede evidenciar hipometabolismo.
DAT‑scan ayuda a confirmar alteración dopaminérgica.
Exclusión de Alzheimer, delirium y trastornos psiquiátricos.
No existen biomarcadores definitivos; diagnóstico es mayormente clínico.
treatment: Inhibidores de colinesterasa (donepezilo, rivastigmina) para síntomas cognitivos.
Levodopa en dosis bajas para síntomas motores, vigilando alucinaciones.
Antipsicóticos de segunda generación (quetiapina) solo si alucinaciones graves, con precaución.
Intervenciones no farmacológicas: terapia ocupacional, rutinas estructuradas y ambiente seguro.
complications: Deterioro funcional que lleva a dependencia.
nursing_care: Evaluar nivel de conciencia y fluctuaciones cada turno.
Prevención de caídas: ambiente libre de obstáculos, calzado antideslizante.
Administrar medicamentos según orden y observar efectos adversos.
Promover actividad física ligera y ejercicios de equilibrio.
Facilitar comunicación clara, usar preguntas cerradas y repetir información.
patient_teaching: Explicar la naturaleza fluctuante y la importancia de mantener rutinas.
Instruir a cuidadores sobre manejo de alucinaciones (reorientación, ambiente tranquilo).
Educar sobre seguridad en el hogar y prevención de caídas.
Fomentar adherencia a la medicación y reporte de efectos adversos.
Promover actividades cognitivas y ejercicio regular.
Sugerir apoyo psicológico y grupos de soporte para pacientes y familiares.

en.summary: Neurodegenerative disorder characterized by fluctuating cognitive decline, visual hallucinations, and parkinsonian symptoms.
key_points: Attention fluctuations are more pronounced than memory loss.
Visual hallucinations and sleep disturbances are distinctive signs.
Motor symptoms can be mistaken for Parkinson’s disease.
Clinical diagnosis supported by neuroimaging and dopamine testing.
Treatment combines cholinesterase inhibitors and careful antipsychotic management.

pathophysiology: Accumulation of Lewy bodies (α‑synuclein) in cortical and subcortical neurons.
Disruption of neurotransmitters, especially dopamine and acetylcholine.
Neuronal degeneration produces cognitive deficits and motor symptoms.
Alertness fluctuations due to altered reticular activating network.
risk_factors: Male sex with slightly higher prevalence.
Family history of dementia or Parkinson’s disease.
signs_symptoms: Fluctuating cognitive decline, worse in attention than memory.
Sleep disorders with REM movements without atonia.
Rigidity, tremor, and bradykinesia similar to Parkinson’s.
diagnostics: Clinical assessment with MMSE or MoCA and consensus criteria.
Neuroimaging (MRI/CT) shows minimal atrophy; SPECT/PET may reveal hypometabolism.
DAT scan helps confirm dopaminergic dysfunction.
Exclusion of Alzheimer’s, delirium, and psychiatric disorders.
No definitive biomarkers; diagnosis is mainly clinical.
treatment: Cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine) for cognitive symptoms.
Low‑dose levodopa for motor symptoms, monitoring hallucinations.
Second‑generation antipsychotics (quetiapine) only if severe hallucinations, with caution.
Non‑pharmacologic interventions: occupational therapy, structured routines, and safe environment.
nursing_care: Assess level of consciousness and fluctuations each shift.
Fall prevention: obstacle‑free environment, non‑slip footwear.
Administer medications as ordered and observe adverse effects.
Promote light physical activity and balance exercises.
Facilitate clear communication, use closed questions, and repeat information.
patient_teaching: Explain the fluctuating nature and importance of maintaining routines.
Instruct caregivers on hallucination management (reorientation, calm environment).
Educate on home safety and fall prevention.
Encourage medication adherence and reporting of side effects.
Promote cognitive activities and regular exercise.
Suggest psychological support and support groups for patients and families.

related_to: visual hallucinations that may cause disorientation

interventions.action: Assess and record alertness and orientation every 4 hours.
interventions.rationale: Detect fluctuations that increase fall risk.

interventions.action: Keep environment free of obstacles and use handrails in hallways.
interventions.rationale: Reduce opportunities for tripping and falling.

interventions.action: Place bed in low position with raised rail.
interventions.rationale: Decrease severity of potential falls when attempting to stand.

interventions.action: Teach caregiver calm reorientation techniques during hallucinations.
interventions.rationale: Prevent impulsive responses that could cause injury.

interventions.action: Apply safety devices (safety belt, gentle restraints) only when necessary and with consent.
interventions.rationale: Prevent falls without unnecessarily restricting mobility.

outcomes: Increase activity tolerance by 20% in 2 weeks
Maintain sufficient energy for basic ADLs

interventions.action: Plan activities in 5‑10 minute blocks with scheduled breaks.
interventions.rationale: Allows patient to conserve energy and avoid exhaustion.

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and fatigue level before and after activity.
interventions.rationale: Identify overload and adjust exercise plan.

interventions.action: Encourage stretching and passive mobility twice daily.
interventions.rationale: Improves flexibility and reduces rigidity without demanding much effort.

interventions.action: Educate caregiver on respecting rest periods.
interventions.rationale: Prevents exacerbation of intolerance and reduces fall risk.

interventions.action: Record activity tolerance and progressively adjust duration.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates safe progression and evaluation of improvement goal.
